title: Cross-Cultural Adaptation and Validation of the European Portuguese Version of the Problem Gambling Severity Index.
abstract: The Problem Gambling Severity Index (PGSI) is widely used to assess the prevalence of problem gambling on a community level. No cultural adaptation or psychometric validation of the instrument has been conducted for European Portuguese. The sample comprised 171 individuals, aged 18 to 75 years old. Internal consistency, construct validity, and criterion validity were assessed using McDonald's omega (ω), the South Oaks Gambling Screen, and gambling disorder criteria based on the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, respectively. The unidimensional structure of the PGSI was assessed through confirmatory factor analysis (CFA). Cut-off point for problem gambling was established based on the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) and precision recall (PR) curves. The Portuguese version of the PGSI has excellent internal consistency (ω = 0.89). Construct validity (ρ = 0.515, p < .001) and criterion validity (ρ = 0.482, p < .001) were established through significant positive correlations. CFA confirms the one-factor solution as the best fit for the PGSI (CFI = 0.995). ROC and PR curves estimates point to different cut-off scores, with the cut-off of eight being the recommended threshold for problem gambling. Our data suggest that the European Portuguese version of the PGSI is a reliable tool for assessing gambling severity.
